questions.topic: Selling shares and reinvesting; change in income
questions.question: Subhash sold x shares of Rs. 100 paying 10% dividend at a discount of 25% and invested the proceeds in Rs. 100 shares paying 16% dividend, quoted at Rs. 80 and thus increased her income by Rs. 2000. Find the value of x.
questions.solution: Case I: M.V. = 100 − 25 = Rs. 75; sale proceeds = 75x. Old dividend = x × 10% × 100 = Rs. 10x. Case II: number of new shares = 75x/80 = 15x/16; new dividend = (15x/16) × 16% × 100 = Rs. 15x. Increase in income = 15x − 10x = 5x = 2000 ⇒ x = 400 shares.

questions.topic: Word problem: product of consecutive multiples of 3
questions.question: The product of two consecutive natural numbers which are multiples of 3, is equal to 810. Find the two numbers.
questions.solution: Let the numbers be x and x + 3. x(x + 3) = 810 ⇒ x² + 3x − 810 = 0 ⇒ (x + 30)(x − 27) = 0 ⇒ x = 27 or −30. x is natural, so x = 27. Numbers: 27 and 30.

questions.topic: Cyclic quadrilateral and alternate segment theorem
questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral. RT is a tangent, ∠PQR = 80° and ∠SRT = 50°. Find the angles of ΔPSR.
questions.solution: ∠PSR = 180° − ∠PQR = 180° − 80° = 100° (opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral). ∠SPR = ∠SRT = 50° (angles in alternate segment). In ΔPSR: ∠PRS = 180° − (100° + 50°) = 30°. Angles of ΔPSR: ∠P = 50°, ∠S = 100°, ∠R = 30°.

questions.topic: Slope, equation of a line and perpendicular line from a graph
questions.question:
In the figure, O is the origin, A(4, 4), B is a point on the x-axis (at x = 2), and the line BC is perpendicular to OA, meeting the y-axis at C.
i) Find the slope and equation of OA
ii) Write down the co-ordinates of B
iii) Find the equation of BC ⊥ to OA
iv) Hence, write down the co-ordinates of C
questions.solution: i) Slope of OA = (4 − 0)/(4 − 0) = 1; equation y = x, i.e. x − y = 0. ii) B = (2, 0). iii) Slope of BC = −1 (product of slopes of perpendicular lines = −1); y − 0 = −1(x − 2) ⇒ x + y = 2. iv) C is where BC meets the y-axis: x = 0 ⇒ y = 2, C = (0, 2).

marking_points.point: Slope of BC = −1 and equation x + y = 2

Plot A(8, −4) and B(6, 2). Locate points A' and B' images of A and B in the x = 4.
i) Write their co-ordinates

iii) Find its area
questions.solution: Reflection in x = 4: (x, y) → (8 − x, y). i) A' = (0, −4), B' = (2, 2). ii) AA' (y = −4, length 8) is parallel to BB' (y = 2, length 4) and AB = A'B', so ABB'A' is an isosceles trapezium. iii) Height = 2 − (−4) = 6; Area = ½(8 + 4) × 6 = 36 sq. units. questions.topic: AA similarity and area ratio
concepts: ratio of areas of similar triangles
questions.question:
D and E are two points on sides AB and BC of ΔABC such that ∠EDB = ∠ACB.
i) Prove that ΔABC ~ ΔEBD.
ii) If BE = 6 cm, EC = 4 cm, BD = 5 cm and area of ΔBED = 9 cm², calculate the a) length of AB b) area of ΔABC.
questions.solution: i) In ΔABC and ΔEBD: ∠B is common; ∠ACB = ∠EDB (given). ∴ ΔABC ~ ΔEBD (AA). ii) Corresponding sides: AB/EB = BC/BD = AC/ED. BC = 6 + 4 = 10. a) AB/6 = 10/5 ⇒ AB = 12 cm. b) ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔEBD) = (AB/EB)² = (12/6)² = 4 ⇒ ar(ΔABC) = 4 × 9 = 36 cm².
questions.figure_desc: Triangle ABC with A at top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right; D on AB and E on BC joined by DE; BE = 6 cm, EC = 4 cm, BD = 5 cm; ∠EDB marked equal to ∠ACB.

questions.topic: Two angles of depression from a lighthouse
questions.question: From the top of a light house, the angles of depression of two ships on the same side of the light house are 60° and 45°. Find the height of the light house, if the distance between the ships is 36 m. Answer to the nearest metre.
questions.solution: Let AB = h be the lighthouse, C the nearer ship (60°) and D the farther ship (45°), CD = 36 m. In ΔABC: tan 60° = h/BC ⇒ h = √3·BC. In ΔABD: tan 45° = h/BD ⇒ h = BC + 36. ∴ √3·BC = BC + 36 ⇒ BC = 36/(√3 − 1) = 18(√3 + 1) ≈ 49.18 m. h = 49.18 + 36 = 85.18 m ≈ 85 m.

questions.topic: Recasting capsule-shaped solid into a cone
questions.question: A solid consists of a cylinder with hemispherical ends of radius 3 cm. Its full length is 14 cm. If this solid is melted and shaped into a cone of radius 6 cm, find the height of the cone.
questions.solution: Cylinder length = 14 − 2 × 3 = 8 cm. Volume of solid = πr²h + 2 × (2/3)πr³ = π(9)(8) + (4/3)π(27) = 72π + 36π = 108π cm³. Cone: (1/3)π(6²)H = 12πH = 108π ⇒ H = 9 cm. (The handwritten key treats the solid as having only one hemispherical end, cylinder 11 cm, and gets 9.75 cm; with hemispherical ends at both ends as stated, the height is 9 cm.)

No. of students: 4, 7, 15, 13, 5
questions.solution: Convert to class boundaries: 49.5–59.5, 59.5–69.5, 69.5–79.5, 79.5–89.5, 89.5–99.5 (kink on x-axis). questions.topic: Componendo and dividendo
questions.question: Using the properties of proportion, solve for x, given (x⁴ + 1)/(2x²) = 17/8.
questions.solution: By componendo and dividendo: (x⁴ + 2x² + 1)/(x⁴ − 2x² + 1) = (17 + 8)/(17 − 8) ⇒ (x² + 1)²/(x² − 1)² = 25/9 ⇒ (x² + 1)/(x² − 1) = 5/3 (taking positive root). Again C&D: 2x²/2 = (5 + 3)/(5 − 3) = 4 ⇒ x² = 4 ⇒ x = ±2. Check: (16 + 1)/(2 × 4) = 17/8 ✓. (The handwritten key writes 5/4 instead of 5/3 after taking the square root and gets x = ±3, which does not satisfy the equation: (81 + 1)/18 ≠ 17/8. Correct answer x = ±2.)

questions.topic: Loci in a circle: perpendicular bisector and angle bisector
questions.question:
Use ruler and compass for this question. Construct a circle of radius 4.5 cm. Draw a chord AB = 6 cm.
i) Find the locus of points equidistant from A and B. Mark the point where it meets the circle as D.
ii) Join AD and find the locus of points which are equidistant from AD and AB. Mark the point where it meets the circle as C.
iii) Join BC and CD. Measure and write down the length of side CD of the quadrilateral ABCD.
questions.solution: Draw circle radius 4.5 cm and chord AB = 6 cm. i) Locus of points equidistant from A and B is the perpendicular bisector of AB; it meets the circle at D (on the major arc). ii) Locus of points equidistant from AD and AB is the bisector of ∠DAB; it meets the circle at C. iii) Join BC, CD: CD ≈ 5.1 cm (key accepts about 5.0 cm ± tolerance).

marking_points.point: Circle and chord AB; perpendicular bisector giving D

questions.topic: Identity with square root
questions.question: Prove that : √[(1 − sinA)/(1 + sinA)] = secA − tanA
questions.solution: LHS = √[(1 − sinA)(1 − sinA)/((1 + sinA)(1 − sinA))] = √[(1 − sinA)²/(1 − sin²A)] = √[(1 − sinA)²/cos²A] = (1 − sinA)/cosA = 1/cosA − sinA/cosA = secA − tanA = RHS.

questions.topic: Ogive: median, lower quartile, count above a value
questions.question:
The daily wages of 80 workers in a project are given below.
Wages (in Rs): 400–450, 450–500, 500–550, 550–600, 600–650, 650–700, 700–750
No. of workers: 2, 6, 12, 18, 24, 13, 5
Use a graph to draw an ogive for the above distribution. Use your ogive to estimate:
i) the median wage of the workers.
ii) the lower quartile wage of the workers.
iii) the number of workers who earn more than Rs. 625 daily.
questions.solution: Cumulative frequencies: 2, 8, 20, 38, 62, 75, 80 plotted against upper limits 450 … 750 (start at (400, 0)); join with a smooth curve. i) Median = n/2 = 40th worker ⇒ ≈ Rs 604–605. ii) Lower quartile = n/4 = 20th worker ⇒ Rs 550. iii) At Rs 625 the c.f. ≈ 50, so workers earning more than Rs 625 ≈ 80 − 50 = 30.

marking_points.point: C.f. table and ogive plotted with scale
